A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L-MTP work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark performance, inference speedups, prediction-accuracy analyses, simulations, and appendix training-loss curves.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a comparison of prediction-head counts and leap strides in Appendix D, Table 3.

M1.justification: The multi-head architecture, two-stage training objectives, backward-looking decoding, and tree attention remain unchanged. Table 3 tests different values of the existing n and k parameters without introducing a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: The training corpora and math, code, general-task, and prediction-accuracy evaluation coverage remain unchanged. New Table 3 reuses the eight benchmarks from Table 1; the added personalization references do not introduce personalization experiments.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds seven-head MTP as an explicit longer-horizon comparison variant alongside four-head MTP. This is a limited expansion within the existing baseline family; the original NTP, MTP, F-MTP, and Medusa-based comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added appendix comparison evaluates MTP with n=7 and L-MTP with k=3, n=3 alongside the existing configurations. These introduce head-count and stride controls. The previously reported model suite, datasets, metrics, training budgets, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a targeted ablation comparing adjacent and leap prediction with alternative head counts at a seven-token horizon. It tests whether increasing MTP's horizon helps and whether fewer, more widely spaced L-MTP heads remain competitive. Earlier supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 7 retains the same across-model box plots, and Table 3 adds point estimates without a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds results for MTP n=7 and L-MTP k=3, n=3, with averages of 51.82 and 52.35. Its four-head MTP and default L-MTP rows repeat existing averages of 52.79 and 53.75. All 216 numerical entries in Table 1 and the Table 2 speedups are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Assumption 2, Theorem 3, and the Appendix A proof retain their mathematical content. Several displayed expressions are split and renumbered in v2, but no assumption, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of broader prediction supervision, improved task performance, and faster inference, including the 22% improvement and up-to-fourfold speedup statements. The appendix addition supports the existing contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: The new Table 3 discussion proposes that skipping some distant predictions reduces accumulated noise relative to predicting every adjacent position. This mechanism explanation is new. Existing interpretations concerning myopia, data quality, scalability, and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code release to providing a GitHub repository URL and stating availability. Appendix F still promises a future release, leaving inconsistent wording. Existing pseudocode, architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, and data-processing instructions are retained; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds six introductory references, numbered 16–19 and 24–25, concerning personalization and reasoning or abstract thought. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against adjacent MTP and speculative decoding remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. Limited additions include the Appendix D discussion, an introductory personalization mention, acknowledgements, a corresponding-author designation, and a short expansion of Figure 2's caption.

P2.justification: The document switches globally from the wider preprint layout to the narrower NeurIPS format, changing typography, spacing, figure/table sizing, float placement, and equation wrapping. Table 3 is added. Figure 5(c) also corrects the reversed legend: dashed blue becomes k=1 and solid red becomes k=2. The twelve figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 control provides limited additional evidence about leap placement versus prediction range. Correcting Figure 5's reversed legend removes a misleading inconsistency, and the code URL improves access information, although Appendix F retains conflicting release wording. These are useful gains while the method, proof, and main empirical evidence remain stable.
